To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
speculative prices fluctuated in the past and they will do so in the future.

speculative markets are "trend-following" and "trend-reversing" in the sense that prices tend to follow the direction of a long-term trend, but reverse that trend at some point, and that the long-term trends are composed of a succession of short-term waves.

the "invisibility" of the hand of the invisible hand is due to the fact that the hand is not a single hand but rather many hands, all working in concert to produce a long-term trend that is the result of a succession of shorter term trends, and all of which are based on short-term fluctuations that are the product of many individual hands.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the question of how short-term market fluctuations produce long-term trends in the exchange rate.
the question how short-term price waves accumulate to produce long trends.
the question of how a "trending" pattern develops in speculative markets and why the "invisible hand" of the market mechanism fails to produce a balanced market.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the market is "not rational" but "not random" either.
the market is not a "random walk", but a complex dynamical system.
the invisible hand" of market forces does not produce a "natural" balance of prices but rather a "natural" imbalance.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the price fluctuations in speculative markets are the result of the interaction between two different kinds of market forces: (1) the market's "trending" forces, which are responsible for the long-term price fluctuations, and (2) market's "balance forces", which are responsible for short-term price fluctuations.
the "invisible hand" of Adam Smith is indeed invisible.
the "invisible hand" of Adam Smith is not a "natural law", but a statistical phenomenon.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the price dynamics of speculative markets is not random, but is driven by a self-reinforcing process that generates long-term trends from short-term price waves.
price trends in speculative markets are not a result of a rational market equilibrium.
short-term fluctuations are not random, they are driven by long-term trends.
